job.style: a step-by-step explanation of a process

passage: When you pick up a packaged food item, the first thing to check is the ingredient list, which is always arranged by weight. The ingredient listed first is the one present in the largest quantity, not the smallest. Many people mistakenly think that if sugar is not the first item, the food is low in sugar, but manufacturers often use different names like corn syrup or dextrose to hide added sugars. Next, look for the FSSAI logo, which confirms that the manufacturer follows food safety standards, but remember that this logo does not mean the food is necessarily healthy or nutritious. You must also check the nutrition facts table carefully. Pay attention to the 'serving size' because the nutrient values listed are usually for one serving, not for the entire packet. If you eat the whole packet, you are consuming multiple servings. Finally, look for the vegetarian mark, which is a green dot inside a green square. If a product does not have this specific mark, you cannot assume it is vegetarian, as it might contain hidden animal-derived ingredients. Always read the label thoroughly to understand exactly what you are eating instead of relying on marketing claims like 'natural' or 'no added sugar' on the front of the package.

items.evidence: The ingredient listed first is the one present in the largest quantity, not the smallest.
items.q: A biscuit label lists flour first and salt last. Which is present in the larger amount?
options: Flour, because it is listed first
Salt, because it is listed last
Both, since labels list equal amounts
Salt, because small items are listed first
items.explain: Ingredients are listed by weight, so the first one, flour, is present in the largest quantity.

wrong.why: reverses the order of the list
thinks the first ingredient is the smallest amount

items.evidence: Many people mistakenly think that if sugar is not the first item, the food is low in sugar, but manufacturers often use different names like corn syrup or dextrose to hide added sugars.
items.q: Sugar is not first on a label, yet the food is very sweet. Why?
options: Sugar may be listed under other names
Sweetness comes only from the first item
Sugar is always listed last by law
Corn syrup has no sugar in it
items.explain: Makers may use names like corn syrup or dextrose, so sugar can hide further down the list.

wrong.why: thinks sugar must be first if the food is sweet
thinks sugar has a fixed place on the list
thinks only the word sugar means sugar

items.evidence: Next, look for the FSSAI logo, which confirms that the manufacturer follows food safety standards, but remember that this logo does not mean the food is necessarily healthy or nutritious.
items.q: A packet of chips has the FSSAI logo. What can you conclude about it?
options: Its maker follows food safety standards
It is a healthy and nutritious snack
It has no added sugar or salt
Its licence number matches all other foods
items.explain: The FSSAI logo shows safety standards are followed, but it does not mean the food is healthy.

wrong.why: thinks the FSSAI logo means healthy
thinks the logo guarantees no sugar or salt
thinks the licence number is the same on all products

items.evidence: Pay attention to the 'serving size' because the nutrient values listed are usually for one serving, not for the entire packet.
items.q: A packet holds three servings. Ria eats all of it. What does she get?
options: Three times the nutrients listed per serving
Exactly the nutrients listed on the table
One third of the nutrients listed
Nutrients that are not shown on the label
items.explain: Table values are for one serving, so eating three servings gives three times those nutrients.

wrong.why: thinks the whole packet gives the same as one serving
divides instead of multiplying the servings
thinks the table does not cover the nutrients

items.evidence: If a product does not have this specific mark, you cannot assume it is vegetarian, as it might contain hidden animal-derived ingredients.
items.q: Why should you not treat a food with no mark as vegetarian?
options: It may contain hidden animal-derived items
The green dot is used only for sweets
Unmarked foods always contain animal products
The mark shows the food has no additives
items.explain: Without the green dot mark, the food might contain hidden animal-derived ingredients, so you cannot assume it is vegetarian.

wrong.why: reads the mark as only for some foods
thinks the green dot means no additives
